characters.continuity: DC Comics - Kingdom Come and associated comic appearances
characters.summary: Kingdom Come Batman is an older, physically broken Bruce Wayne who relies on an advanced mechanical exoskeleton to support his body. He commands a network of automated bat-drones and security systems from the Batcave and leads the Silent Cavalry, prioritizing advanced strategy, defensive fortifications, and tech-driven oversight over direct physical combat.

techniques: Command of Batman-themed robots and robotic drones
Martial arts and detective skill (limited by his injuries)
Leading the Silent Cavalry and his metahuman agents

mechanisms: Battle suit built by his employees

weaknesses: Severe physical degradation and spinal damage without the exoskeleton
Aged physical condition and reliance on spinal exoskeleton support
limitations: Dependent on a mechanical exoskeleton to mitigate physical deterioration and spinal damage
Injuries limit his own fighting; he stays mostly confined to the Batcave in old age
characters.formDifferences: Represents an aged, physically deteriorated Bruce Wayne who requires a heavy mechanical exoskeleton to walk and fight, relying entirely on automated drones and tactical command.

sources.supports: Kingdom Come Batman depiction, exoskeleton dependence, and use of automated security drones.

Surgically attached exoskeleton and later back brace due to years of injuries; Batman-themed robots protecting Gotham and robotic drones; battle suit; martial arts, detective and computer skills; mostly confined to the Batcave.

feats.claim: Employed an army of automated security robots and drones to monitor and police Gotham City.

notableResults.note: Confronted Superman during the final conflict at the Gulag with assistance from his allies.

conditional.ability: Enhanced physical strength and unhindered mobility

campaignTags.claim: Operates advanced medical exoskeletons and automated security drones.
Employs high-tech utility belts, surveillance systems, and drones.

unknowns: Exact extent of unassisted combat capability given advanced degenerative spinal injuries.

No documented one-on-one fight result in Kingdom Come; the earlier claim of a Kingdom Come #3 loss to Superman was removed because Superman only confronts him verbally (Batman does not fight Superman or Wonder Woman).

characters.earlierSummary: Kingdom Come Batman is an aged Bruce Wayne whose body is so damaged by years of crime-fighting that he depends on a surgically attached exoskeleton. He guards Gotham with Batman-themed robots and drones from the Batcave and leads his own network of heroes (the Silent Cavalry), preferring strategy and command to direct brawling.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Dark Multiverse and main DC continuity crossover events
characters.summary: The Batman Who Laughs is a corrupted Bruce Wayne infected with a concentrated Joker toxin that stripped away his morality while retaining his tactical genius. He employs sadistic psychological warfare, specialized firearms, bladed chains, Dark Metal weaponry, and a precognitive visor, utilizing infected sidekicks known as Rabid Robins.

techniques: Machine guns, knives and a bladed chain
Dark Metal batarangs that bring out a victim's worst self

mechanisms: Dark Metal visor granting a form of precognition

weaknesses: Arrogance and obsession with psychological dominance
Vulnerable to Nth Metal, like other Dark Multiverse inhabitants

depictions.title: DC Comics - Dark Multiverse (Dark Nights: Metal and The Batman Who Laughs)

mobility: Standard peak human athletic mobility enhanced by dark technology
limitations: Dependent on specialized Dark Metal equipment and prepared toxins for extreme encounters
Relies heavily on elaborate planning and subordinate minions
characters.formDifferences: Combines Batman's tactical mastery and intellect with the absolute sadism, lack of inhibition, and chaotic methods of the Joker.

sources.supports: Origins, Dark Metal gear, Ninth Metal visor, and Joker toxin background.

feats.claim: Subdued the Justice League of Earth-0 using specialized Dark Metal cards and contingency gear.
Corrupted multiple Robins into feral subordinates using modified Joker toxin.

notableResults.note: Ambushed the team utilizing prepared Dark Metal vulnerabilities.

notableResults.citation: Year of the Villain: Hell Arisen #4
notableResults.note: Defeated before his final ascension into the Darkest Knight.

conditional.ability: Multiversal awareness and anticipation of enemy moves

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Dark Nights: Death Metal
characters.summary: The Darkest Knight is the ultimate evolution of the Batman Who Laughs after absorbing the brain and power of Doctor Manhattan from a universe-hopping counterpart. Wielding god-like cosmic energy, reality-warping manipulation, and absolute control over Crisis energy, he poses a multiversal-level threat capable of rewriting reality.

techniques: Realigning worlds and deploying his evil Earths

mechanisms: God-like durability derived from Doctor Manhattan's powers

weaknesses: Vulnerability to anti-crisis energy and paradoxes of equal cosmic scale
Can be overpowered by Superboy-Prime's blows and by Wonder Woman in a sustained fight

depictions.title: DC Comics - Dark Nights: Death Metal

limitations: Dependent on sustained access to absorbed multiversal energy streams
Power partly depends on absorbed Crisis energy and on the Mobius Chair rigged to feed him
characters.formDifferences: Replaces standard human gear and peak physical traits with godlike, reality-warping Doctor Manhattan powers and boundless Crisis energy.

sources.supports: The Darkest Knight origin, absorption of Doctor Manhattan powers, and cosmic feats.

notableResults.note: Overpowered and destroyed the cosmic creator entity.

Trapped Perpetua in fragments of the Source Wall and killed her, realigning Prime Earth.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Modern Post-Crisis, New 52, and DC Rebirth
characters.summary: Batwoman (Kate Kane) is a highly trained military veteran and martial artist who wages war on crime in Gotham City using high-tech impact armor, a bladed gliding cape, stun gauntlets, and specialized throwing blades. She relies on rigorous tactical discipline, firearms proficiency, and exceptional hand-to-hand combat skills.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Modern Post-Crisis, Teen Titans, and DC Rebirth
characters.summary: Beast Boy (Garfield Logan) is a green-skinned shapeshifter who can transform into any animal he has ever seen, including extinct prehistoric beasts such as Tyrannosaurs, as well as insects and marine life. He rapidly adapts to combat environments by gaining the physiological traits, flight capabilities, and water-breathing abilities of his chosen forms, supported by a rapid regenerative healing factor.

techniques: Large predator and prehistoric forms (T. rex, elephant)

mechanisms: Healing factor (recovers from bullet wounds, burns and broken bones in seconds)
Evasion through flying or small forms

weaknesses: Retains human consciousness and vulnerabilities when caught off-guard in animal forms
Psychological stress during prolonged or extreme transformations
Retains human psychological vulnerabilities and animal instincts if overwhelmed

limitations: Must have previously seen an animal to replicate its form successfully

Larger forms used to physically exhaust him
